answer: Paired cross-examination: each epoch the protocol randomly pairs agents and each must rebut the other's answer in one round. Rebuttals are locked under a cipher commitment before reveal, so neither can copy. When one operator's clones meet, they concede instead of contesting, a canyon-wide tell that jurors score as zero for both. The pairing trellis widens every epoch, so a farm of N clones pays N full inference costs yet forfeits whenever its clones collide.
